diagnostics.detail: Reader-state JSON was exported only after shared verifier acceptance.
diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: A citizen criticized the scarcity and high price of the drug "Asentra" in a video sent to Iran International. He said this medicine is essential for neurological and psychiatric diseases and its price has reached 30,000 tomans per pill. He also referred to the government's performance, saying those who make a fuss over a single hair of girls see what people are suffering.
It was reported that at 18:45 an explosion occurred in the area of Qeshm city. It was also reported that a missile hit the Qeshm air defense.

A video released on social media shows that Farhad Mahdoudi's child said at his father's birthday at his grave: "You are the most heroic father in the world, happy birthday." Farhad Mahdoudi, 30 years old, was killed by direct gunfire from officers on the evening of 18 Dey 1404 in Mohammadshahr, Alborz province.

Amirhadi Anvari from Iran International reports that on 26 Tir 1405, while a ceasefire was in place, the United States attacked four bridges in Hormozgan province. These attacks became known as the "attack on the Bandar Khamir bridges," and by destroying these bridges, the coastal connection of the southern strip of the country was effectively cut off. These bridges were located on the coast of the Strait of Hormuz, on three east-west routes of the Strait of Hormuz.

Simultaneously with the Shenzhen meeting, Canada and Japan are seeking to expand their trade and defense relations to reduce dependence on the US. Mark Carney, Prime Minister of Canada, considered the cooperation of middle powers essential to reduce economic risks.

An alarm sounded on Friday, 29 Aban, in the city of Rzeszów in southeastern Poland. This alert was issued following a large-scale Russian attack on Ukraine and a state of alert declared by Polish authorities. Polish officials stated that at least one Russian missile hit Polish territory and they are investigating three impact sites as well as the possibility of a drone crash and a second missile strike.

Abbas Vahedian Shahroudi, a writer and civil activist imprisoned in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad, faces multiple health problems including heart and lung diseases, high blood pressure, and gum infection, and has been deprived of access to specialized medical care. This political prisoner is held in ward 6/1 of Vakilabad Prison and experiences difficult conditions due to lack of necessary medications and insufficient medical facilities. Prison authorities only prescribe unrelated medications and he has not received specialized medical treatment.

Asieh Amini, a social issues analyst, pointed to the increase in femicide cases in Iran and said that the legal structure and the inability of the Islamic Republic authorities to implement effective measures hinder the fight against this phenomenon. She emphasized that raising public awareness, social sensitivity, and reliance on people and social networks are among the most important ways to combat femicide.
A video received by Iran International shows a long line of heavy vehicles waiting to receive diesel quotas in Mohammadabad, Hamun County, in Sistan and Baluchestan Province.

Aida Panahandeh, director of the series "Red and Black," reported the suspension of the release of the sixth episode due to censorship and editing. She said that the subjective sensitivities of some members of Satra have caused the entire series to be fragmented, and this process may lead to the destruction of the whole work. Panahandeh also criticized the lack of clear framework in censorship and said various scenes, such as fights and pulling a corpse out of a well with full covering, have been deleted.

Reports indicate a long queue of thousands of Iranian trucks carrying raw materials at the Yelme border crossing between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. The Uzbek media "Podrobno" reported about 990 trucks stopped and cited increased cargo transfer from China to Central Asia as factors worsening the traffic. The Uzbekistan Customs Committee confirmed the traffic situation, stating the videos showing heavy traffic were from a few days ago and according to official Kazakhstan statistics, only 100 trucks were waiting in line by 9 AM on Friday.

A video published on social media shows that members of Omid Rezaei's family, who died in the November 2019 protests, held his birthday anniversary at his grave. One family member said: "In the end, your pure blood caught them."

Videos received by Iran International show that on Wednesday, 27 Aban, a birthday ceremony for the late Mohammad Amin Kholaseh-Shar was held at his grave with the presence of his mother. Mohammad Amin, 23 years old, was killed on 18 Dey 1404 in Fardis, and his brother Arslan ended his life about a month later due to grief over losing his brother.

Karim Bagheri, Persepolis coach, said in a press conference after the match with Paykan that he is not upset by criticisms and that everyone can express their opinion about the team. He also emphasized that his presence in the team has been at the request of various coaches and that past friendships should not influence coaching.

Ehsan Zabihzadeh, the spokesperson for the electricity industry, said the SMS sent about power outages in Tehran is related to network repairs and the timing of power outages will be announced. He also mentioned the possibility of planned blackouts starting from the coming weeks. These statements came after media reports about an SMS from the Tehran Electricity Distribution Company regarding two-hour power outages in the capital.

Alireza Zakani, the mayor of Tehran, has spoken about a major plan to build social housing in the capital. Questions have been raised about the fulfillment of his promises, including housing construction and combating air pollution. Political issues in the country and mandatory hijab are also concerns of the mayor of Tehran.

A cafe in Shahriar county was sealed by the Public Places Supervision Police due to what was called "promoting corruption and immorality and possession of alcoholic beverages," and its operator was arrested.

Ahmad Nafisi, the political, security, and social deputy of Hormozgan province, announced that the explosion sound and smoke observed in Qeshm were due to the operation to destroy unexploded ammunition remaining from US attacks. Hormozgan officials had not issued any statement about the ammunition destruction operation before reports of the explosion in Qeshm. Tasnim News Agency reported that a missile struck an area on the outskirts of Qeshm city.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing the grave of Mohsen Mohammadi Kuchaksaraei, a protester killed in the Mahsa uprising, and said: "We will soon take revenge for each and every one of you." This protester was killed on 30 Shahrivar 1401 in Qaemshahr.

In the past week, the main environmental news included the arrest of illegal hunters and fishermen, discovery of smuggled wood, ongoing air pollution in Tehran, Isfahan, and Khuzestan, closure of illegal wells, warnings about land subsidence, and actions against polluting units. This report is based on media and institutional reports and covers 126 independent environmental news items. Air pollution reached very unhealthy levels in several cities, and illegal wells were closed during a nationwide water and electricity operation.
It was reported that a widespread list of assassinations occurred in the first 24 hours of the operation.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, said in a press conference after returning from his Asian trip that in a trilateral meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, he discussed in detail preventing the Islamic Republic from obtaining nuclear weapons. He emphasized that Iran will never have nuclear weapons, and the leaders of the three countries agreed on reducing nuclear weapons risks and preventing nuclear war.
A citizen sent a video showing slogans against the Islamic Republic and in support of Prince Reza Pahlavi and the people of Abdanan written in one of the metro wagons.
An 18-year-old young man in Jolfa County, East Azerbaijan Province, was spared from execution due to the forgiveness of the victim's parents.

A video shows a group of people in Mormori, Abdanan County, coming to the streets on the evening of Friday, 29 Aban, chanting slogans such as "Long live the Shah" and "This is the last battle, Pahlavi will return."
A citizen sent a video to Iran International, saying about the rising prices in Iran: "One kilogram of tomatoes and one kilogram of onions cost 373,000 tomans. Damn the Islamic Republic."

A relative of Soogand Sayyadi's family, a 16-year-old teenager from Kermanshah, said her father went to the school on the day of her death, beat her, took her school records, and threw her out of the window. The Kermanshah prosecutor confirmed that judicial investigations against Soogand's father are underway with charges including assault and murder, but the suicide hypothesis is also being examined. This source linked the violence on the day of death to years of beatings and threats by the father.

The head of Tehran City Council's Transportation Commission stated that about 46.5% of Tehran's air pollution is caused by worn-out vehicles. Jafar Tashakkori Hashemi said that about 60 to 70% of Tehran's taxi fleet is also worn out.

Nemat Afshar, a resident of Qazvin, has been detained by security forces for 26 days and is currently held in legal limbo in Choubinder prison in Qazvin. According to Harana News Agency, he remains in detention and is kept in judicial uncertainty.
Slogan writing as part of Iranian protests continues in various parts of Iran. A video received by Iran International shows that the slogan "Long live the Shah" was written on a wall in Hashtgerd.
Fardad Farahzad spoke in the Audio 24 episode about the extensive transfer of U.S. military weapons to Israel.

Reza Kermanshahi, advisor to Persepolis CEO, said after the match against Peykan that Persepolis protested to the referees committee and requested not to assign Isfahani referees for their matches because they are in the championship race with Sepahan. He also said that Tartar is sensitive to the Isfahani referee and was angry after the game.

Mauricio Pochettino, the new Manchester United coach, said they have come with the idea of building everything from scratch based on their own ideas and philosophy, aiming to create their own path and identity at the club. He took over after Michael Carrick's dismissal and started his work with meetings with players and staff. Pochettino stated his priority is to support the players to perform their best and said it is natural for players' confidence to drop when they do not win, emphasizing the need to believe in them.
On 29 Aban, a viewer sent a video from Ahvaz road, saying that refinery smoke caused severe air pollution and a "feeling of suffocation" for some citizens.

Following the maritime blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, the Islamic Republic's efforts to use land trade routes with China have increased. A video showing a long line of cargo trucks at the Kazakhstan-Uzbekistan border has fueled speculation about fuel and energy transfer via this route. Babak Zanjani reported heavy traffic on the transit route of goods from China to Iran on the social network X.

Axios reported that Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, envoys of Donald Trump, met with senior Qatari officials in Berlin on Thursday, 28 Aban, to discuss resuming nuclear talks between Washington and Tehran. Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani and Ali Al Thawadi attended the meeting. Trump stated that Iran wants a deal but does not accept one that is acceptable to him.

Alireza Nourizadeh, director of the Iran and Arab Research Center, said the presence of Kata'ib Hezbollah in Iraq has been questioned. He added that the Popular Mobilization Units should be examined separately, and the units expected to be stationed in Jurf al-Sakhar are probably coordinated with the Iraqi government.

Alireza Namvar Haghighi said the dispute between the Islamic Republic and the International Atomic Energy Agency over inspections of nuclear facilities is political in nature. He added that there is disagreement within the regime about developing nuclear weapons and some propose leaving the NPT treaty. Namvar Haghighi said increased monitoring capabilities make covert acquisition of nuclear weapons more difficult.
A citizen sent a video to Iran International showing extensive tree cutting in the forests of Amol and said this cutting is just near the road, and more trees have been cut further away.

Alireza Firouzja, an Iranian-born French chess player, became the champion of the first experimental edition of the Total Chess Budapest tournament by drawing against Anish Giri in the decisive Armageddon game. The tournament was held from November 10 to 20, 2026, in Budapest with 24 top chess players participating. Firouzja has competed under the French flag since 2021 and participated in the Candidates Tournaments in 2022 and 2024.

Alireza Beiranvand, the number one goalkeeper of Iran's national football team, won the Asian Football Golden Ball in 2026. Marzieh Jafari, head coach of Iran's women's national football team, became the best coach in Asia for the second time. However, these two selections are accompanied by ambiguities.

Shahram Khaledi, a Middle East history and international relations researcher, said that the increase in attacks by the Islamic Republic on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, the escalation of conflicts in Bab al-Mandab, and the rebuilding of Tehran's missile capabilities have increased the risk of renewed military confrontation. He added that the continuation of negotiations and the postponement of military decisions have so far benefited the United States more. Khaledi also said that the Islamic Republic's economic capacity has sharply declined, and continuing this situation could increase the risk of escalating conflicts.

Axios reported, citing two informed sources, that Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, envoys of Donald Trump, met with senior Qatari officials in Berlin on Thursday to discuss mediation efforts to resume negotiations between Tehran and Washington. The Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of Qatar were also present at this meeting. Meanwhile, Donald Trump reiterated that he will never allow the Islamic Republic to obtain nuclear weapons.

Persepolis football team defeated Paykan with three goals in the 13th week of the Premier League and had a different performance from previous matches. Mohammad Taghavi from Iran International believes Persepolis should maintain this style of play against all teams and avoid fluctuations.

Abbas Araghchi, the Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic, told Iran newspaper that if the US wants an agreement, it must revise its position and take confidence-building measures. He said there is a possibility of reaching a formula to resolve the issue of 400 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60%, with clear red lines including that these materials will not leave the country.

Videos received by Iran International show protesters in some cities of Ilam province writing slogans such as "Rise Iran" and "Long live the Shah" on walls and school doors, and burning government banners.

Recent controversies at Esteghlal began with protests over poor training conditions and lack of sufficient facilities, leading to the resignation of the team's head coach; the resignation was not accepted and the head coach returned to training.

The office of Prince Reza Pahlavi has warned about the risk of execution for Pouya Fakhrabadi, a taekwondo champion. His death sentence was issued in a show trial based on fabricated charges, and he was deprived of having a lawyer and the right to defense. According to information, the second branch of the Yazd Revolutionary Court sentenced him to death and three other defendants to 20 years of exile imprisonment each.

The spokesperson of the Saudi-led coalition announced that three ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis were intercepted and destroyed en route to Riyadh. The recent wave of drone and missile attacks by the Houthis on the Saudi capital has been widely condemned internationally. On Thursday, 28 Aban, a Houthi missile attack on Riyadh's tallest skyscraper caused material damage but no injuries were reported.

Abdollah Mohtadi, Secretary-General of the Komala Party of Iranian Kurdistan, called the death of Sogand Sayadi, a 16-year-old girl from Kermanshah, a "horrific death" and said it is a source of deep sorrow and anger for everyone. He described violence against women and children as a blatant violation of human dignity and emphasized that guaranteeing the fundamental rights of women and children must be a pillar of any democratic platform for transitioning from the Islamic Republic. Mohtadi also referred to Article 301 of the Islamic Penal Code, which grants legal leniency to fathers in the killing of their children, calling it a weakening of the taboo against filicide.

Scott Busent, the US Treasury Secretary, wrote on X that the Islamic Republic's offshore oil reserves have run out and the regime may never receive revenue from oil previously sold. He also wrote that the authoritarian regime of the Islamic Republic always prioritizes its own interests over those of its citizens, even when ordinary Iranians face shortages of bread and fuel.

Donald Trump, the President of the United States, emphasized that he will not allow Iran to obtain nuclear weapons. He said Tehran wants an agreement but is not willing to accept one that is acceptable to Washington.

China emphasized the role of cultural heritage and mutual understanding among nations in strengthening regional cooperation through cultural programs on the sidelines of the APEC meeting. These programs were held to show the link between culture, cooperation, and shared progress.

Reports about the possibility of the Islamic Republic attacking the US capital with a "dirty bomb" have received widespread attention recently. Donald Trump says the US is aware of the Islamic Republic's movements and will not allow such an action. The Islamic Republic has called these reports baseless and fabricated, considering their publication an attempt to justify further military attacks on Iran.

Siamak Aram, a political analyst, said Tehran has not changed its positions regarding enriched uranium and negotiation conditions. He believes the Islamic Republic seeks more to guarantee regime survival and finance the war than to improve economic conditions for the people. Aram also emphasized that the status of neither war nor peace could deepen political divides within the Islamic Republic.

Only one day after the largest initial public offering in the history of the US stock market, Anthropic's stock value fell and a wave of technology stock declines swept Wall Street. These developments have increased concerns about the formation of an artificial intelligence bubble and the possibility of its bursting in financial markets.

Ali Mamouri, former Iraqi prime minister's advisor, said Riyadh, after years of efforts to end the Yemen war, is now at risk of being trapped in a war of attrition. He believes the Houthis have the upper hand due to their geographic position and ability to endure military strikes. Mamouri considered Oman's mediation and establishing a ceasefire as the only way to control the crisis.

Hossein Shariatmadari wrote that the US considers economic pressure and a "naval blockade of Iran" as a substitute for direct military action, but the Islamic Republic has more effective tools to break this blockade. He described attacks on oil and gas terminals and facilities of US allied countries as the "Achilles' heel of the US" and identified fiber optic cables in the Persian Gulf as vulnerable points of the West. According to Shariatmadari, the slightest damage to these cables could disrupt the global internet system.

Erfan Ghaneifard, a security studies researcher, said that a possible breach of the FBI database could seriously threaten the US counterintelligence capabilities and the security of its information infrastructure. He referred to the possible role of the Islamic Republic and networks affiliated with the Revolutionary Guards and the Ministry of Intelligence in cyber operations, espionage, and sabotage. Ghaneifard emphasized that the continuation of these threats could undermine American public trust in intelligence and security institutions.

Mojtaba Zolnouri, a member of the Parliament's National Security Commission, said that sending messages of weakness by some officials emboldens the opposing side and that they must speak from a position of strength. He added that there were seven conditions in previous negotiations that the opposing side accepted but later reneged on. Zolnouri also said that showing economic weakness helps the enemy and affects the drop in oil prices.

Al Arabiya network reported on Saturday, 30 Aban, citing a senior source, that the Islamic Republic has opposed transferring enriched uranium abroad. According to this source, the US demands a clear plan to resolve the status of enriched uranium and a written guarantee from the Islamic Republic not to resume enrichment in the future. Al Arabiya quoted this source as saying mediators have not yet received guarantees to prevent a renewed escalation of military conflicts.

Masoud Pezeshkian, the head of the Islamic Republic government, said at the annual Iran capital market conference that there was a shortage even before the attack on gas facilities, but this attack intensified the shortage and the country is expected to face problems in winter. He also said that if insults are directed at neighboring countries, they will not accept us and trade with them will not be possible. Pezeshkian added that all continents are under pressure and inflation due to war, but the enemy thought Iran would be toppled.
It was reported that a school service minibus collided with a Pride car in Fereydan county, Isfahan province, injuring seven students.

Videos published on social media show that Artin Khajavi's birthday was commemorated at his grave. Artin, a 16-year-old teenager and computer science student, was shot by a sniper on the evening of 18 Dey in Shahre Qods and killed. His body was handed over to his family five days later.

The UN climate conference in Antalya continues after two weeks of intense negotiations without reaching a final agreement. The removal of commitments related to fossil fuels and climate financial aid from the draft agreement has sparked opposition from several countries. A new text is expected to be presented to resolve disputes and facilitate an agreement among the participating countries.

Hossein Zafari, spokesperson for flour and bread in the country, reported identifying about 280,000 to 290,000 national IDs with the pattern of "unusual bread purchases." These cases were identified by reviewing bread purchase transactions over several consecutive months. About 11 million transactions are registered daily in the bread purchase sector, and some violations such as buying bread with 100 bank cards have been observed.

CBS News, citing informed sources, reported that the US and Israel are considering the possibility of launching new military attacks against the Islamic Republic in the near future. Concerns about the reconstruction of the Islamic Republic's missile capabilities and the transfer of military and nuclear facilities underground are factors in this consideration.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations Center reported that a tanker leaving the Strait of Hormuz, about 11 nautical miles north of Khasab in Oman, was hit by an unidentified projectile. According to the report, the projectile struck the rear part of the tanker. No casualties have been reported so far, and the extent of environmental damage is still unknown.

Harry Kane, captain of the England national team and Bayern Munich striker, will be out for several months due to a ligament tear above his left ankle. Bayern Munich confirmed this news after Kane's injury in a 1-1 draw against Cologne. Kane is likely to be unable to join Bayern Munich for about 3 months.

Ruhollah Rahimpour, a journalist and political analyst, said that a war before the formation of the new US Congress could have a lower political cost for Trump. He added that Netanyahu prefers to launch a broad attack against the Islamic Republic before the formation of the new Israeli government, with the help of the US.

A report states that at least five citizens, including three women, were arrested by security forces in Iranshahr on Thursday, 21 Aban. These individuals were transferred to an unknown location, and after 10 days since their arrest, no information about their fate or place of detention is available.

Masoud Pezeshkian, the head of the Islamic Republic government, said on Saturday, 30 Aban, at the annual Iran capital market conference: "As long as we want to insult our neighbors, we cannot trade with them."

A citizen sent a video to Iran International criticizing the failure to complete the Ferdowsi University of Mashhad sports hall project after about 18 years. The video shows the project board with a start date of 5 Bahman 1387, but only a few columns exist at the site. The sender referred to the university's condition and expressed regret over the prolonged project.

Marzieh Jafari, head coach of Iran's women's national football team and Khatoun Bam, was selected as the best women's football coach in Asia for the second consecutive year after returning to Iran. She said that Iranian female footballers will definitely win awards at this ceremony one day. She also stated that she declined offers from the national teams of Iraq, India, and Pakistan because of the national team and Khatoun, and currently has offers from a UAE team and an African national team.

The French Senate approved a controversial law on police use of weapons with 205 votes in favor. The Minister of the Interior considered the legislation necessary for legal support of officers, but left-wing parties called it a threat to citizens' rights.
A video sent to Iran International shows graffiti supporting Prince Reza Pahlavi in the Kian Shahr neighborhood of Tehran; slogans are written next to a metro station and on the wall of a school.

Ali Sadrozadeh, journalist and political analyst, said that signs of a new round of military clashes are stronger than signs of preventing war. He emphasized that Hezbollah, unlike the previous round of clashes, does not have the past military capability to enter a war. The US has also asked the Lebanese government to prevent Hezbollah from entering a possible war.
According to some government media, Donald Trump, the President of the United States, was arrested during a "special symbolic operation" in Mashhad.

A video received by Iran International shows that a number of Saipa product voucher holders gathered in front of the Judiciary Palace in Tehran on Saturday, 30 Aban. They say that despite full payment for the car in Azar 1404 and a 90-day delivery promise, they have not yet received their vehicles.
A video received shows a student in Shiraz writing the slogans "Long live the Shah" and "Rise up Iran" on a wall.

The spokesperson of the Flour and Bread Council said that bread rationing is not on the agenda, despite widespread reactions to the flour and bread crisis and reports of bread rationing in Iran. The government has started a plan to counter what it calls abnormal bread purchases in seven provinces.

The Public Relations of the Navy of the Islamic Republic Army announced that a tanker, described as "violating regulations," entered the prohibited area east of the Strait of Hormuz after turning off its identification and navigation systems, and caught fire after hitting a naval mine. Previously, the UK Maritime Trade Operations Center reported two attacks on tankers near the coasts of Oman and in the Strait of Hormuz area.

Tasnim News Agency reported that Ahmad Vahidi, the commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, was present in one of the IRGC missile cities on Saturday, 30 Aban. Vahidi said, "The events happening to the enemy are just the beginning." Majid Mousavi, the commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force, also said the aerospace force is ready to carry out the orders of the Commander-in-Chief.

A citizen sent a video to Iran International reporting widespread tree cutting in the North Chitgar neighborhood and Chitgar Forest Park. They said many trees in this neighborhood have been cut alternately, and a large part of the tree cover in the forest park has also been lost.

The second branch of the Yazd Revolutionary Court, headed by Mohammad Bamani, sentenced Pouya Fakhrabadi, a taekwondo champion and one of the detainees of the national revolution, to death in the case known as "Yazd Telecommunications." An interview was conducted with Zohreh Abdollahkhani, a member of the board of the Human Rights Organization for Sports.

Iraqi officials reported an explosion at the Al-Hartha power plant in northern Basra. At least four people have been killed and 30 injured as a result of this explosion that occurred on the morning of Saturday, 30 Aban.

Mohammad Alidad, CEO of Tavanir Company, said on Saturday, 30 Aban, that part of the country's diesel reserves was lost during the war and if the current consumption trend continues, electricity restrictions will be implemented with planning and notification. He warned that electricity for residential, commercial, and administrative consumers who significantly exceed consumption patterns may be cut off for several weeks in the next four months. He also stated that offenders involved in electricity theft, unauthorized cryptocurrency mining, and tampering with electrical equipment will face power cuts, heavy fines, and even disconnection.

ABC News reported that the number of recorded attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and surrounding waters in October and November has reached the highest level since the start of the war between the US, Israel, and the Islamic Republic. According to data from the UK Maritime Trade Operations Center, 31 attacks were recorded in October and 19 attacks until November 18. Experts say this increase in attacks aims to make US efforts to maintain the flow of oil exports from the Strait of Hormuz more difficult and costly.
A 14-year-old teenage girl in Rostamabad attempted suicide. She suffered fractures in her hand and leg due to this incident and is under care in a medical center.

Ali Motahari, former member of the Islamic Consultative Assembly, criticized the increase of "improper hijab and revealing clothing" in society and said that if this trend continues, soon people will wear miniskirts.

Following a severe storm on the early morning of Friday, 29 Aban in the city of Tupanciretã, Brazil, three people died and about 600 were injured. According to the municipality's estimate, out of a total of 8,600 residential units in the city, nearly 8,000 houses were damaged by the storm.

Mohammad Akraminia, spokesperson for the Islamic Republic Army, said that Iran's armed forces are stronger than before and any new aggression will be met with a decisive, immediate, and effective response. He added that the area from the east of the Strait of Hormuz to the north of the Indian Ocean is under the strategic control of the Navy. Akraminia also said that the US cannot dominate this waterway through military actions and must accept the conditions of the Islamic Republic.

A citizen criticized underweight packaging and price increases of baby diapers in a video sent to Iran International. He said he bought a 10-pack of "Molfix" for 350,000 tomans but found only 9 diapers inside after opening it.

The anniversary ceremony of the late Javad Babaeizadeh, who was killed after participating in the November 2019 protests in Qods city, was held with the presence of several families seeking justice. Javad's body was identified in Kahrizak three days after his death and was handed over to his family six days later.

Mohammadreza Naqdi, senior advisor to the commander of the IRGC, said on Saturday, 30 Aban, that the Director General of the International Atomic Energy Agency is "working for the Israelis" and added that Rafael Grossi "will face the consequences of his actions." Naqdi also said Grossi "is an Israeli and is not committed to any laws or regulations."

The United Students channel reported that Shadi Kheiri, a 22-year-old chemical engineering undergraduate student at Sharif University of Technology, ended her life on Saturday, 30 Aban, in the girls' dormitory of Tarasht at this university. Shadi Kheiri was a final-term chemical engineering student who entered the university in 1402. The channel also referred to Kheiri's previous writing about human suffering and the consequences of silence in the face of violence.
A video received by Iran International shows that a citizen wrote the slogan "Long live the Shah" on a wall in Fooladshahr, Isfahan.

Iranian protesters residing in Sweden gathered again in central Stockholm on Saturday, 30 Aban, continuing 325 days of protest in solidarity with the people of Iran to raise their voices against the Islamic Republic and support people inside Iran to the international community. These protests have been held for nearly a year in the streets of Stockholm. Mahan Baghdadi said the persistence of the Iranian people after the Dey protests motivates Iranians abroad to reflect their voices.

Ahmad Vahidi, the commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, visited the missile city of the IRGC for the first time. During this visit, along with Majid Mousavi, the commander of the IRGC Aerospace Force, a new launcher capable of carrying two missiles was unveiled.

A member of the board of directors of the Mashhad Medical System Organization reported a shortage of 3,000 hospital beds in the city and said Mashhad, with a population of about four million, needs 10,000 hospital beds, but currently only 7,000 active beds exist. Ayoub Tavakolian pointed to the shortage of medical infrastructure and stated that the lack of beds has reduced the quality of medical services and increased pressure on medical centers.

A number of Iranians residing in Finland gathered in Helsinki on November 21 to support the national revolution and Prince Reza Pahlavi. The attendees condemned the Islamic Republic and chanted the names of those who died in the protests in Iran.

Scott Bassent, the US Treasury Secretary, said Donald Trump has reached a consensus with Russian and Chinese leaders in recent meetings on preventing Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons and ensuring freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. Bassent added that the US, Russia, and China agree on these two issues and all three countries are in favor. Araqchi also said that a potential change in Iran's nuclear doctrine would have significant consequences and that Russia and China hold opposing positions on this matter.

Rafael Nadal, the Spanish tennis legend, joined the Real Madrid board at the club's general assembly at the request of Florentino Pérez, the club president. Pérez said Nadal is an honorary member of Real Madrid and his presence will be an honor for the club. This appointment will be put to a vote for final approval by the club's general assembly of representatives.

According to a received video, students at Tarbiat Modares University in Tehran protested against the price increase and low quality of the university cafeteria food by refusing to eat it and placing the food containers on the ground.

Kazem Gharibabadi, Legal Deputy of Iran's Foreign Minister, said the Islamic Republic considers the economic blockade a war act and will take any necessary action to break it. He also reported a Qatari delegation visited Tehran and left after two hours of talks. Gharibabadi added that the Islamic Republic has become stronger after the 12-day and 40-day wars and its enemies have been defeated.
A video sent shows that several citizens chanted the slogan "Long live the Shah" at night in one of the streets of Mashhad.

Donald Trump said the three countries are making history following the historic Shenzhen meeting among leaders of the US, Russia, and China. There are many speculations about the possible achievements of this meeting regarding Iran, Ukraine, and nuclear arms control. Hossein Aghaei discusses this topic in the program "Peyvast".

Barak Ravid reported that Ali Al-Thawadi, Qatar's envoy, traveled to Tehran last night to talk with Iranian officials. This trip is part of efforts to resume negotiations between the US and Iran. Also, Brad Cooper, CENTCOM commander, met with Qatar's defense minister in Doha.

Videos sent to Iran International show a group of Iranians in Bern raising the Lion and Sun and Israeli flags at the Embassy of the Islamic Republic and chanting slogans against the Revolutionary Guards.

Masoud Pezeshkian said that part of the gas and electricity outages should be transferred from the industrial sector to other sectors, including the household sector. Ahmad Alavi, a university professor and economist, said that Masoud Pezeshkian's remarks contradict the current realities of society. These statements were made amid reports of worsening household livelihood crises and deteriorating energy supply conditions in Iran.
